newsitem.title: USA: KN Energy TransColorado pipe gets FERC ok.
newsitem.headline: KN Energy TransColorado pipe gets FERC ok.

text.p: KN Energy Inc said Thursday the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission has approved the first phase its joint project to transport natural gas from Colorado's Piceance basin.
Other equal partners in the TransColorado Gas Transmission Co are the El Paso Energy Corp of El Paso, Texas and the Questar Corp of Salt Lake City.

The pipeline will begin in northwestern Colorado and continue 292 miles south to Blanco, N.M., where it will connect with lines to Texas, California and elsewhere, said Questar spokesman Curt Bennett. It will have a capacity of 300 million cubic feet per day, KN Energy said.
The first phase is construction of about 25 miles in New Mexico and is scheduled to be completed in December.
An application to obtain FERC approval for phase two, which covers the remaining distance to the Piceance basin in northwestern Colorado, has yet to be filed, Bennett said.
"Phase II is dependant on market support, whether a sufficient number of (natural gas) producers contract for space," Bennett said.
